title: Stellantis taking Unifor to court over obstruction of environmental work
summary: The ongoing dispute over the sale of Stellantis' Brampton, Ont., assembly plant is heading to court, as the automaker has filed a lawsuit alleging Unifor is impeding an environmental assessment…

blocks.text: The ongoing dispute over the sale of Stellantis' Brampton, Ont., assembly plant is heading to court, as the automaker has filed a lawsuit alleging Unifor is impeding an environmental assessment necessary to the transaction.
Documents filed in Ontario Superior Court of Justice last Thursday, Stellantis seeking injunction
· Posted: Nov 24, 2026 4:03 PM EST | Last Updated: 27 minutes ago

In documents filed last Thursday in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, Stellantis said it is seeking an injunction requiring the union, its national president Lana Payne and Unifor Local 1285 plant chair Ardis Snow to refrain from blocking the Brampton plant and preventing work at the site.

The company wants the court to declare that the union has trespassed at the facility and "obstructed the lawful entrance to and exit from the premises," which has restricted Stellantis’ ability to provide access to environmental consulting firm Pinchin Ltd.

A statement of claim says Pinchin was retained by Roshel — the armoured vehicle manufacturer that agreed to buy the idled Brampton plant from Stellantis — to carry out environmental work starting Nov. 9. The allegations have not yet been tested in court.

However, Stellantis says that morning, union representatives blockaded entrances to the plant with trucks, pylons and individuals carrying Unifor flags and that Unifor told the automaker it wouldn't let Pinchin personnel or equipment through.
Unifor national president Lana Payne says in a statement that the union "has been demonstrating in support of Canadian jobs at the Brampton plant throughout the past year."
"We continue to fight for the jobs of our members and for the entire Canadian auto industry," Payne said.
"The sale of the plant to Roshel is unacceptable to our union. And we will continue to work with all parties to try to get a different outcome.”
